svg.title: Where duplicate sends come from
svg.desc: A channel worker's steps on a timeline: receive the message, claim a dedupe key, call the provider, the provider accepts, record SENT, then acknowledge the message. A crash before the provider call is safe because the retry finds no send. A crash after the provider accepted but before SENT is recorded is the duplicate window, because the retry cannot know the provider already accepted the message. A crash after recording SENT but before the acknowledgement is caught by the dedupe record.

g.text: At-least-once delivery: what a crash at each step causes
One channel worker processing one send (notification, channel, device)
You cannot close the red window with your own database alone:
the provider's accept and your SENT write are two systems with no shared transaction.
Shrink it and soften it instead:
pass a provider idempotency key where the API supports one
set a collapse id on push so a duplicate replaces the first on the device
keep the window short: no slow work between the provider call and the SENT write
